evidence_quotes: 106 seismic events were recorded globally between 2026-01-26 and 2026-02-16, with magnitudes ranging from 4.0 to 6.1 and an average of 4.64
Tobelo, Indonesia (12 events) and Nikolski, Alaska (11 events) led all regions by event frequency
a magnitude 5.7 at 152.9 km depth on 2026-02-14
a magnitude 4.9 at only 8.5 km depth on 2026-02-12 and a separate event at 1.9 km depth
a magnitude 5.2 event at 189.7 km depth in the Aleutian Islands on 2026-02-15
shallow events (as low as 3.3 km depth near Tobelo on 2026-02-14)
no tsunami flags were recorded for any event in this dataset
criticisms: The report states 'a magnitude 5.2 event at 189.7 km depth in the Aleutian Islands on 2026-02-15' in the Risk Watch section, but the digest places this event as '65 km E of Aleutian Islands, Alaska' — the report simplifies this to 'Aleutian Islands' which is a minor but acceptable paraphrase; however it is slightly imprecise.

The report claims 'roughly 0.6 events per day' for Tobelo — this is a derived calculation (12 events / 21 days ≈ 0.571), which is a reasonable derivation but not explicitly stated in the digest; it is borderline but defensible.

The report mentions the period's maximum magnitude of 6.1 was 'recorded in the dataset' but no sample event in the digest actually shows a 6.1 magnitude event — the 6.1 appears only in summary.max_magnitude. The report does not falsely attribute it to a specific place, so this is acceptable but worth noting.

The report references 'Maluku region' in the Risk Watch section — this is a reasonable geographic inference for Tobelo's location but the term 'Maluku' does not appear in the digest. This is a minor geographic inference rather than an invented place name.
